findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the chemical dish machine was not sanitizing at an effective concentration of Chlorine (10ppm). CORRECTED: PIC determined that the sanitizer dispenser was empty and replaced the dispenser with a new bucket during the inspection. Chemical dish machine was then measured to be sanitizing at effective concentration of Chlorine for warewashing (50ppm). Ensure that chemical sanitizers used in mechanical warewashing are used per manufacturer’s instructions regarding pH.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the front dress prep cooler was not sufficiently cooling and cold holding TCS foods (see Violation #33):

(i) sliced tomatoes (probed 52°F) and shredded lettuce (47°F). CORRECTED: tomatoes and lettuce were voluntarily discarded, as they were prepared longer than 4 hours ago; previously prepped tomatoes and lettuce were taken from the walk-in cooler and placed in ice baths, which will be monitored for cold holding temperatures.

(ii) shredded cheese (52°F) and cooked spaghetti (56°F). CORRECTED: shredded cheese and cooked spaghetti were voluntarily discarded, as they were removed from proper cold holding temperatures longer than 4 hours ago; a new container of shredded cheese was prepared and new packages of cook spaghetti were moved from the walk-in cooler and both were kept in a nearby short cooler that was sufficiently cold holding.

(iii) milk (42°F) and manufactured sauces that require refrigeration (clucked sauce, mayonnaise, and garlic spread - 43°F). CORRECTED: sauces were moved to nearby coolers that were sufficiently cold holding.

Ensure that TCS foods are kept at temperatures of 41°F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed the front dress prep cooler was not sufficiently cooling and cold holding TCS foods. findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Observed that the following freezers had significant ice drip buildup that was falling onto food:
(i) the walk-in freezer. Staff had placed a pan to collect drips, but additional ice drips had formed missing the pan and falling onto food. CORRECTED: PIC moved food away from the fans where the ice is forming and dripping.
(ii) the 2-door standing freezer. CORRECTED: PIC placed a tray directly underneath where the ice drips are forming so that when they defrost they do not fall below onto the food.
Ensure that freezers do not get significant ice buildup, and that the ice does not contaminated the food stored in the freezers.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed hand washing practices at the facility and observed the following:

-- Hand washing frequency is inconsistent from one staff member to another. Obtain and post an SOP for handwashing either from the franchisor or develop a facility specific one, however, all staff must understand when hand washing is required.

-- The facility is short staffed and unable to manage hand washing with busy operations. Two employees and a manager were present on arrival. During this time, inspector observed an employee preparing food at the front grill with a slice of cheese in hand who then returned to the fryers, cheese still in hand, to turn off the alarm (using a glove hand to touch a soiled NFCS) on the fryer. Staffing must be sufficient to ensure that cross-contamination at the facility and two employees plus a manager is insufficient with any significant amount of business at the facility. The employee was immediately instructed to stay in one area, but this is not feasible with only two employees present. Failure to properly staff the store results in an inability to wash hands during appropriate intervals and the separation of activities required to prevent cross-contamination from occurring. Ensure that staffing is sufficient at all times to ensure food safety.

-- Inspector observed an employee return from cleaning activities to food preparation without hand washing between activities. Gloves are NOT a replacement for proper hand washing. When switching activities that result in the potential contamination of the hands, such as cleaning the dining room, gloves must be removed, hands must be washed, and new gloves must be donned before working with food. Ensure that staff is aware that any activities in the dining room such as cleaning, picking up consumer trays, and so forth must be followed by hand washing due to potential contamination from consumers visiting the facility.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Person-in-charge (PIC) has several repeat and/or priority/priority foundation violations during the inspection today. 

PIC advised inspector that the majority of accumulation had occurred prior to her appointment as CFM at the facility which is correct. This violation was observed during the previous inspection and corrective actions were required as of today's date. Further, PIC advised inspector that a list of all areas requiring cleaning was not itemized in the previous report. As noted in the previous report, cleaning is required underneath ALL pieces of equipment in the facility. The PIC must be able to identify areas which do not comply with 2017 FDA Food Code as part of the responsibilities of a CFM. The responsibility for identifying all areas of the facility which require cleaning does not fall on SCDPH but on the facility.

Due to the priority/priority foundation and repeat violations observed during the inspection today, a 30-day follow-up is issued to evaluate the overall state of compliance at the facility. Ensure that no priority or priority foundation violations exist in the facility at that time. Inspector will return on 08/25/2023.

findings.comment:

The crease was still present in the paper towel roll at the end of the inspection indicating that hand washing had not occurred at that sink. 4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the prep cooler along the south wall of the kitchen where sandwiches are made was observed to have temperatures around 50 to 55 degrees F. Temperatures in the prep cooler must be maintained at 41 degrees or below. The facility does not have a time-as-a-control policy which states that items in the cooler are discarded after 4-hours in the prep cooler. The lid to the prep cooler was left open on inspector arrival allowing foods to warm to within the critical range above 41 degrees. Inspector closed the lid during the inspection. Ensure that staff are aware to keep the lid to the cooler closed. If the lid is to remain open and foods are observed to be out-of-temperature, establish a time-as-control policy and discard all TCS foods in the prep cooler at the end of 4-hours. Ensure that ALL TCS foods not covered under a time-as-control policy are kept at 41 degrees or below at all times. A follow-up is issued for 07/28/2023 to ensure cold-holding temperatures in the prep cooler are below 41 degrees and/or establish time-as-control policy.

5-403.12: Condensate drainage and other non-SEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 03/21/2023.

Inspector observed the floors underneath all pieces of equipment in the kitchen to be soiled with grease, refuse and debris. The majority of the accumulation observed during the inspection today was also observed during the inspection on 03/21/2023 prior to the current CFM taking over as person-in-charge (PIC). 

Heavily soiled areas include but are not limited to underneath and behind the cash register counter, the reach-in coolers to the left of the grill, the grill, the steam table, the corner counter reaching to the drive thru, the counter to the right of the drive thru, the fryers, and the prep cooler to the right of the fryers, the double upright fry freezer to the left of the fryers, and the dish machine. Underneath/beneath each of these items (and any others within the kitchen itself not explicitly listed) is large accumulation of soil that has been present since prior to the previous inspection. These areas are required by 2017 FDA Food Code as adopted by the State of Illinois to be clean often enough to prevent such accumulation from occurring. 

The severity of the soil accumulation is of serious concern for the harborage of pests in the future as well as the growth and spread of pathogens as the accumulation worsens. PIC has stated concerns with being able to move the equipment to clean. Food code requires that equipment be constructed in a manner which allows it to be easily cleanable.

A follow-up is issued for 08/04/2023 to allow time for cleaning to occur. Ensure that corrective actions have been taken to bring the facility back into compliance by this date.
